utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for this delay. It's 1D5448. 5498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear a phone ringing. Most likely a mobile one but ... it may be outside the courtroom. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We need page 121 in English version and 119 in B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is incident G-7. It says: "On 4 February 1994, at around 1130 hours, three 120-millimetre mortar shells impacted and exploded in the Dobrinja area, in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street and in a playground in the immediate vicinity of the street." In relation to this incident, the Prosecution submitted the whole file; it's P867. And we would need this document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document, we need English page 22 and B/C/S 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here the location of the incident is stated as Sarajevo, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva and Dz. Nehrua Street. On the covers, we see the Nehru Street but was this explosion in the Dzavaharlal Nehru Street processed? Is it covered in the report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no explosion covered in this report because there was no explosion in that street. There is no information that there had been any explosion there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go back to 1D5498.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 122 in English and 120 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see picture 64. Could you mark on this street plan the Dzavaharlal Nehru Street, which is now called differently?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only I need assistance with this. Dzavaharlal Nehru Street is now called Hamdija Kapidzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we just zoom into this picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would it be better to have only one version --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One version. Yes, let's have English version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I underlined the new name of the street that used to be called the Nehru Street. It's now called Hamdija Kapidzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to reports, where did explosions that were covered by the report happen? Do we know at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know according to the photo documentation explosions happened on the playground in the Mihajlo Pupin Street and in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. Should I mark them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mihajlo Pupin Street is marked by number 466 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next this line will you put number 1. I know it's difficult to draw lines there.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street is marked by number 353. And that should be number 2; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were also explosions next to this garage and at the playground. That would be number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean on the same day or earlier or later, these explosions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're now talking only about this incident and the shells that landed there and that are covered by this photo documentation and the one that was on the screen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please mark the number 1 a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could assist in raising [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, if could you only delete the first one. Now it looks like Z.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we have number 1 on the screen. Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... ask a question. Is it correct that three shells are supposed to have fallen in this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this specific incident, documentation covers three shells. However, material traces and witness statements indicate that four shells fell, and we covered that in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know whether, Mr. Lukic, you'll get the witness to indicate where all of the four fell. Or each one of the four.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- sorry. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, and just continuing with the examination, it would be appreciated in for further examination if the witness mentions something that witness statements or file refers to something, if she could please to or if counsel could please point to the document or statement that is the source of that information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it may be that Mr. Weber was specifically considering the fourth shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's on the line with the question of Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you be a bit more specific about material traces and witness statements for the fourth -- for the -- at least for the fourth shells to start with. And then go to one, two, and three as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Refik Sokolar, who is a policeman, stated that he been injured while sitting in his office in the Nehru Street, and he stated there had been four explosions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And any material evidence, apart from this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And they are covered, described in detail in our expert report and marked in the photo documentation that we had just had on the screen. That four shell is marked there. It's shown in one of the pictures in the photo documentation and I believe we included in the report. That's picture 65. It fell on the edge of the playground. The second one fell practically across the ground for it, opposite the garage and the playground. The third one fell in the Mihajlo Pupin Street next to house number 3, and the fourth fell in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. And that would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would have been the name of the street where the fourth shell fell at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The fourth one fell on the edge of the playground. That is where I put the asterisk. There is a playground there and across the street from it, there is a pedestrian crossing parallel to a garage. One shell fell on the edge of that playground. The second one on the pedestrian path. The third in the Mihajlo Pupin Street. And the fourth in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it known which of these shells caused the injuries to this witness who was in the Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the Hamdija Kapidzic Street. I didn't understand. The witness who stated there had been four shells he was sitting in his office in the building of the police which is currently Hamdija Kapidzic Street. Did you mean him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The shell that injured him -- there is no basis for including it in this incident, especially because the injury he sustained is technically inexplicable, because he explained it came at him through the wall. Like he was injured by shrapnel that reached him through the wall and that is technically impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is the problem that I'm trying to resolve because according to you, there was no shell that fell on that street but, apparently, according to the Prosecution there was. Now you are telling us that somebody who was sitting in his office in that street got injured and there's no explanation for his injury. So I'm trying to find out what could have injured him if there was no shell on that street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, Refik Sokolar was present at the location of the incident not in his office, because there is no technical explanation to support his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... he was not telling the truth when he says he was injured while he was in his office? Is that how --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. And certainly not in the way he described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you have given us an explanation. Thank you. Bye.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark the fourth shell that you explained on this picture.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a bit difficult to mark because they fell very close to one another here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you marked it with number 4.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll skip a few things because of these questions.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we took it as true that Refik Sokolar was injured [Realtime transcript read in error "jurisdiction"] while sitting in his office, which shell would that have been on that day? One, two, three, or four?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be number five. But since it is not stated in any other reports that a shell had fallen there, I don't know why we would take it and include it in our analysis; but if we had, it would have been number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting more confused, ma'am. According to your own evidence, only four shells fell. Where does number five come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lawyer asked me which number it would have been if it had fallen there. I suppose he wanted me to say whether these four shells had anything to do with his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... look at what the lawyer asked. The lawyer said: "If we took it as true that Refik Sokolar was - now the way it looks, it says jurisdiction - "while sitting in his office" - and I suspect that it is intended to say was injured - "which shell would that have been on that day? One, two, three, or four?" He has added no fifth shell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said which number in sequence it would have been but maybe you get it in interpretation. I understood him to asking about the sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what I see here and I understand him to say of the four shells, the one, two, three, and four, which one would have injured him. He is not asking about a fifth one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the answer is none of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I did continue but maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your question on the screen doesn't say so, sir. You don't mention the fifth one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I said, or any other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, now you're testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I can testify on what I said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The testimony on what you said is on the screen and the witness can tell us what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I think that witness told us what we wanted to hear, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you ask for another one, are you tendering this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. Thank you. We would tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Figure 64 on the English version on page 122 of the document 1D5498 with witness remarks will receive the exhibit number D1256, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Weber. Then D1256 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One little correction. The document is not 1D5498 but D5498. I correct myself. I withdraw my comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, from the report, I take it that the witness drew his conclusions on the basis of the Galic testimony which, as far as I'm aware of is not in evidence, or is it? Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to assist; you're correct, Your Honour. However, the individual did provide similar information. I believe it's in P587, e-court page 4, paragraph 18. I'm just pointing this out, so I believe the Chamber has the information from the individual before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We should then interpret the -- I leave it to you, Mr. Lukic, of course, if the witness in the report then refers to a certain portion of testimony then for us to find where we find similar information despite the help of Mr. Weber is -- of course, I don't know whether the witness has looked at that materials or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And you have it in the footnote 319 in the report and I just wanted to invoke that one. But thank you to my learned friend for helping us. That is P568.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was focussing on the pages we are discussing at this moment which is in the ... But let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Subotic mentioned picture 65 from the report and in the same picture we can find in P867, so I would like to have P867 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry to interrupt, but I just wanted to correct while it's quickly on the record: I gave, accidentally, the wrong exhibit number. It's P567, not 587 that I was referring to. Sorry for my interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you just check the transcript and see whether you are transcribed correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, no. I said P567. I incorrectly referred to P587.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in this document that is before us, we need page 126 in English and B/C/S, 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P867, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that the pages you mentioned are not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's from the report. I'm sorry. It's page 22 in P867. And I think only B/C/S version has the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, what can be seen in this photograph on the basis of the police report and photograph 65 from your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the playground looks like and part of the pedestrian path by it where two shells fell, specifically in this area. And the red arrow shows the place where a shell fell on the very edge, and it was not dealt with or mentioned at all in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we also have the English version so we can see the text which is under the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Text is on the page 23, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we be informed about what's happening at this moment? I asked for the corresponding English page. Yes, I think we have the -- yes, I think it was right. What we saw was the text under the photograph, I think. Yes. Okay. There we are. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Ms. Subotic, you told us about this arrow where the shell had fallen and you said that in the report that was not dealt with at all. Which report did you mean? Your own or the police report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the police report that is within this document. I can read the caption, I can read what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It be seen here in English as well.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot see it. Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, in your view what is characteristic in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, what is characteristic is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do have an objection as to, I guess, foundation, in terms of continuing on in terms of an opinion. It's not clear to me right now, because I see the report refers to the shell impact and she's saying the report does not refer to something. So it's really not clear to me what she's exactly saying is or is not referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you assist Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Ms. Subotic, you heard what it is that my colleague Mr. Weber is confused by. Could you please explain to the Court and to me.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now that we're discussing this picture here underneath the text we can all read the caption. This shell was not dealt with at all. And it was not included in the shells that were analysed throughout the police report. That is one thing that is confusing. The second thing that is confusing is why is the street of Hamdija Kapidzic, the former street of Dzavaharlal Nehru, why is that street mentioned all the time when it is 200, 250 metres away from all of this. And, thirdly, there is yet another shell that is marked. Even Barry Hogan recorded that in his film, recorded that place and spoke about it, and although there were injured persons there, this was not analysed at all, not dealt with at all in this report. So out of the four shells that are evidently there according to the material evidence, according to the photo documentation, two were analysed, one was not analysed and it was mentioned though, and the fourth one was not even mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P867, could we briefly take a look at that now, please. It's on our screens, yes, I was just warned by Mr. Ivetic, it's on our screen. If we can have page 98 in English and page 86 in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see the list of persons killed in Dobrinja here on the 4th of February, 1994. There's reference to Jadranka Tendzera - that's number 1 - and on page 77 in the B/C/S version and 82 in the English version. In the B/C/S version, in the middle of the first paragraph, and in the English version, it is the fourth line from the bottom of the page. We see here that Ljusa Sabahudin mentions Auntie Jadranka, that she fell victim there. Where did you locate this place, the one that the young Ljusa refers to?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's the place where it fell, this shell, in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva, the one that was not analysed at all. May I just mention in same document, Sabahudin Ljusa is mentioned both as a fatality and as an injured person. Thankfully, thank God, he is still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes we saw him on that list of killed persons and later on we did see him and he spoke to Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have him in the expert report and that film.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By way of reference, transcript page, Mr. Sabljica, 8155, line 25, to 8156, line 6, that's where he testified and he said that the third location where the explosion took place was not investigated because there were no victims there. So this statement made by Mr. Sabljica, is it correct in your view?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I just go back for a second to one of my previous questions where Mr. Weber assisted. The witness testified that it couldn't be true that the police officer in his office would have been hit by shrapnel because shrapnel does not go through a wall, and a reference was made to what I said, something that's not in evidence, that is the Galic statement. Mr. Weber said we'll find the same in P567. If I read 567 paragraph 18, I read the following -- the witness there describes what happened on 4 February 1994, 11.00 in the morning. He says something about -- he was working in his office and then he said: "The fourth one which injured me landed behind me. Fragments came through the wood in the window." Witness, have you considered whether that shrapnel went through a wall or may have entered the office through the wood in the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regardless of what the obstacle was for that shrapnel, it could not have pierced anything after 250 metres. It is lethal 17 to 20 metres. That's what I have to say about this shell according to our investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you testified that the witness said it went through a wall. My question was: Have you considered, apart yet now from the conclusions, that the witness said at least in what is in evidence that it went through the wood in the window? Have you considered that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where do we find that in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not specify that, but I mean, well, I've already said that shouldn't be taken into account at all in terms of the distance involved. And also the shell did not have any effect in the street of Dzavaharlal Nehru. As far as I can remember, in one of his statements there is mention of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you will be aware that if the witness testified in accordance what she says that witness said in the Galic case and if we find something which at least is somewhat different in his statements P567, that for us to compare we would need the information of both these sources. I just draw your attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Maybe it will be more clear if we have page 20 in English and page 19 in B/C/S from the same report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, what we have before us is a sketch of the scene.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this sketch, how many explosions are marked?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many places are marked in the photo documentation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can the street of Dzavaharlal Nehru be found in this sketch?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Explosion marked as number one, where is it in this sketch?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the edge of the playground. That is how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry. It's the very edge of the pedestrian path. Yes, that's it. It's just marked vis-à-vis the playground as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, we were checking, Your Honour, P568 on page 6, last paragraph, we'll continue checking English version but in B/C/S it says that he was wounded through the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in English it says the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we see the document on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I looked at 567, as a matter of fact, which was mentioned, I think, but if I made a mistake, then -- but you said it's found in 56 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: What is characteristic of this incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at 65 ter 12822. This is the police report. We have Exhibit P0112 but it only has three pages. Therefore, we are going to work with this entire document. We need page 17 in B/C/S. In the English version, there is no picture.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could be concluded that it's from the same tube because of the same azimuth, identical azimuth, and the firings were a couple of seconds of each other. But it also could be that the guns were placed in formation.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that it depends, of course, on the crew. But that is the usual interval between two firings from the same tube: One minute.

utterances.text: Could you fall could you mark the arc with a number 1.

utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.text: And could you mark where you said if the centre of the explosion would be here, there would have been no snow. And then mark that with number 2.

utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I marked the snow. The snow. That's number 2. And the centre of the explosion, I'm going to mark it now.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document here that is before us now. Except that it's further. Just a moment, please. Also on the sketch. It is marked as number 2, the actual scene. Maybe it's easier for us to follow it on the sketch.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that these are certain objects that were either underneath the stall that were used for selling I mean, quite simply it's a market-place, isn't it? So as you can see for yourselves, the picture is unclear so it is hard to see what it is exactly.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this crater is a lot bigger and also it doesn't have a characteristic image as such, and since these objects are in this arc that is contrary to the place that we marked with number 3, and since there is this black part on the left-hand side, the only thing that can be concluded -- also we should take into account that this dispersed snow is in the left-hand part of the image and also black and it gets lighter and lighter and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This fuse, is it related to the first or second explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This fuse is related to the explosion that occurred in place number one, that is, Petra Kocica. So not the one that we discussed a moment ago, the next one, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had this projectile arrived in Petra Kocica Street would it have been possible to get this unactivated fuse?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. It initiates the explosion and it's the first one that explodes and falls apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to page 166 of your report in English and page 162 in B/C/S. It is the shelling of the water line in the elementary school of Simon Bolivar. I'm going to ask you briefly, the police report, I'm going to ask you briefly what you found to be characteristic of this particular case?

utterances.text: In this case, we found an amazing amount of inconsistency when the police report was written and also the crime-scene investigation report. So we had to make a huge effort in order to establish what this was all about. I'm speaking of the figures that are inconsistent, the analysis that is inconsistent, north is wrong, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we please take a look at 104 now. That is actually the sketch of the scene. 165 is the page number. 169 is the page in English. You told us that north was marked incorrectly. Traces of the explosion, what about them? Are they marked; and, if so, where and how?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sketch is not going to be very helpful for us. We can just illustrate what I mentioned a moment ago. You see here, if we add all of this up, the error is 1 metre. It is 470 and 3.2 that are added. 515. The sketch that is the other part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not sure where the witness is explaining that from the sketch. If it could be made clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please resume, Witness, and tell us exactly what you saw on the sketch as you explained it to us, where it is for us to be found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this sketch of the scene, 3.2 metres is the height of the wall. And the length --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. 3 -- no, let me see. 3.2 metres is the height of the wall. Where do we find that on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vertically, 3.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am afraid that we can't see -- what is this -- first of all, what is this exactly? Is it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The height of the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, could we have a look at the title of picture 104, which is visible in the -- in B/C/S, we can see it but not in the English. Could we just move one page forward in the English? Okay. It's the sketch of the scene at the Simon Bolivar elementary school. We can go back now. Now, does this depict a surface or does this depict -- what exactly does it depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see the area of the wall and according to this sketch, that's where the 122-millimetre shell exploded. And we see these measurements that were made. And if you do the appropriate calculation now on the basis of Pythagoras --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second. I see to the left, I see -- and that's not translated "pogled A - A." We still do not know whether this is a frontal sketch of what you see before you or whether it's a projection from above on what can be seen on the ground. Could you first explain to us what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The technician showed 3.2 metres of the height of the wall. You see it's a vertical projection because the pump is vertical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. Just as we are looking at each other now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you then please explain what is depicted in the entire sketch above this wall, as you indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any construction on top of the 3 metres 20 where it reads 10 metres 40. 10 metres 40. Oh, yes. 10 metres 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the height of the gym and above that wall, there were windows that disappeared during some fire. That's what the report says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this is the front view of a building, if I understand you well, or a construction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. If you look at the picture at the very beginning, you will see it is 102. You can see these windows, if you look at that picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's all fine. But then I would have expected, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Ivetic would have taken us to 102 first to know what we're looking at -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move away from this sketch, can you please indicate where we can find the wrong indication north, as you said?

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Picture 106 and 105. Paragraph 119 in our expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with the sketch we see on the screen; correct?

utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. It is the next sketch that is also contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: Can I also ask for clarification. On the wall above that is 10.10, we see rectangles with lines drawn in them. What are those? And then they are cut in the middle.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are columns. And when you cut through that, it just means that it's less than the dimension. I mean, technically. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, even the broad rectangle on the left, is that also a column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That could be a wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you're saying the break there, it means it's not the full length of the hall. It's broken just to fit the picture in here on the piece of paper? This -- this what you've described as technical method of doing things.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- I still have some difficulties in understanding what it is all about. Could we go to figure 102, which is at -- in your report a few pages further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 168 in English and 163 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we have a look at that picture and then later we move again to 104. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if possible in discussion of figure 102, could we have some foundation just in terms of the timing when this photograph was taken. I don't see it clearly indicated in the report.

utterances.text: Okay. We may ask the witness. Now -- the witness still doesn't see it, I think because in the B/C/S it's still 104. Could we go to 102. I mean figure 102, which is in the B/C/S, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 163. Could we enlarge the picture slightly. Could we do the same for the English. Now, Witness, could you tell us exactly -- we looked at a sketch in figure 104. utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the gym --

utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Bolivar. --

utterances.text: 169 in English and --

utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 165 in B/C/S.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague and I recorded it when we were in 2010, in April, visiting sites in Sarajevo. By approval of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.text: Yes. April 2010. Taken by you, yourself.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But the year is right. That satisfied, I take it, your curiosity, Mr. Weber, for the time being. The marked page of the report in the B/C/S version would receive what number, Madam Registrar?

utterances.text: D1260, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. And I think we now can get back to the earlier pages you mentioned. I think it was 169 and for the English and 165 for the B/C/S. Perhaps we leave it as it is for the time being, that we have the sketch next to the photograph. Could you now better explain to us, Witness, what we are seeing. The wall is 3 metres 20 high. Could you describe on the photograph what you meant by the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between the gym and the place where they drew water, between these two spaces was this wall. It's inside. It's not outside. You can't see it from outside. What did I mean to say? There is a complete inconsistency in the data provided here. Let me give you an example. We are looking at this parameter, 5 metres and so many centimetres and we have the measurement for the wall where the shell impacted and here on this sketch is -- it's 320. If we use the Pythagorean theorem, which we indicated below the picture, you get the height of 2 metres 100, not to mention that in another document in this package it is said that the height of this wall is 4 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Could you again explain how Pythagoras says that the picture is wrong? Could you take us -- we have the height of the wall which is 320 and you compared that, you linked that to the 5 metres 15. Now tell us what is wrong there? I mean, the hypotenuse is usually longer than one of the sides so that seems not to surprise. Where does it go wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if under Pythagoras theorem, from these two measurements, 515 and 417, you calculate the hypotenuse, it's no longer as indicated here. Instead, it's 1. -- or 2.5 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Actually, you're saying us that the 475 times 475 plus 320 times 320 is not -- is not 515 times 515. That's Pythagoras. Okay. Did you make the -- let's see -- well, we can check that, that's easy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see what you now mean. I understand what you are arguing here, what your conclusion is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I put another question. You just one minute ago you said the wall was inside and can't be seen on this photograph. What do you mean by "inside"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Inside this school there is a partition wall between the gym and the room where the water sink was, the fountain was, where people drew water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't fully understand. Where in the photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the photograph, 110 and 111, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question about this before we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question to you is, ma'am, if you look at the picture on the right side, not the sketch, the picture itself, from the ground to the roof of that building, what is the measurement? Is it 3.2 that you were talking about earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Now it's not the same as it looked then, but it's 10.10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, in fact, this picture doesn't help us at all. It's not the same building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this photograph does assist us. Let us just see how it looks in the photo documentation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're saying, I'm asking you what is the measurement from the ground to the roof of this building? You are not answering my question. Can you give me the measurement, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the sketch it should be 10.10 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then where is the 3.2 that is below the 10.10 on this building, on this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That should be here, if we are looking at the photo that we took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you should it should be here. I don't know what you're talking about. I don't see your screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the usher assist and [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... oh, yes, I understand. We are talking about the photograph that we took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... photograph that is on the screen before us. Which you saw you took in 2010.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That should be somewhere at the level a bit higher than the boundary of these windows. If 10 metres is to the top, 3 metres is approximately up to one-third.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And where is the wall with the height of 320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is the question we are asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's inside between the room where people drew water. There was a pump there and the gym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I'm asking you again, ma'am, what is the measurement of the height of this building from the ground, as we look at it, to the roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The height of this building should be 10.10 metres up to the roof. The level of the ceiling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, do I understand you to be saying that 10.10 as we see it on the sketch on the left includes the 3.2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it includes 3.2. That's the height of the gym. And we wrote it in the report. It includes those 3.2 metres and that's the height up to the ceiling. Not looking from the outside at the roof but inside up to the ceiling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand your argument much better now. Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic, I'm done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's break time. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to put one question to the witness. Still with respect to the photograph we have in front of us and this sketch on the left side, you said the photograph was taken in 2010. The sketch was drawn much earlier. Have you any information how the situation was before you took this photograph? That means much before the rebuilding of the gym of the school. Where was the wall at that time, the wall with the height of 3 metres 20 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, here in the photo documentation made by the investigators on the spot, it's all visible, the position of the wall and the dimensions of the wall, et cetera. We used that for our analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And if I refer you again to the photograph taken by you in 2010, have you -- can you describe -- you said the wall is now at least at that point in time inside the gym. Was it previously outside the gym?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the description in the document, it was between the gym and this other room. That means that it was a partition wall inside the school. That's what I conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But then I don't understand your description of the sketch on the left side of the screen. You said, If you look from outside to the building, then you see first the wall and behind the wall the structure of the building with the columns and the openings of the -- where previously the windows have been.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's quite possible that it could be an outside wall, but according to the documentation, the gym is on one side, and, on the other side, there was this room containing - and it's written exactly in the documentation - that there were windows that shattered during a fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Windows between two rooms. That means one side --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the windows that were between these two rooms, between these two pillars that you can see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I see. There's no more clarity ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those windows, in any case, did not exist when that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This I understood. But, still, I don't quite understand where the wall was and what the purpose of building a wall between two rooms could have been, but I stop here and leave it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you one other question about still the sketch and what you say underneath. You are referring to the 5 metres 15 centimetres and the 4 metres, 17 centimetres. Could you tell me exactly where you find the 4.17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above the edge of the wall, beginning with the left end, up to the place where the shell exploded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4.17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I, as a matter of fact, but please correct me when I'm wrong, I see something which looks to me as very much 4.70. Could you please have a look at that time? Perhaps it could be slightly enlarged still further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's written 4.70. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But for your calculations you used 4.17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems I made a mistake. I have to check. Or maybe I only made a mistake while writing here. I have to check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now I see that the explosion is, you say, at 320. And the height of the wall is also 320. Does mean that it was just at the edge and do you know that, or how do you know that? I mean --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it have been let's say just 10 centimetres above the top of the wall or 15 centimetres. Could you tell us exactly how you have an explosion exactly at the edge of the wall and whether you were able to verify that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. First of all, the crime-scene technician recorded that it was on the edge of the wall. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But could you conclude from that photo documentation whether it was the centre of the explosion was exactly at the edge of the wall or whether it could have been 5 or 10 centimetres lower or perhaps 15 on a height of 320?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already said it was precisely on the edge of the wall on the decorative plaster work which lines the edge of the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take us to any photograph that supports that interpretation of these facts.

utterances.text: 110 and 11. Okay. I have a look at those.

utterances.text: Page 170 in B/C/S and 175 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 110 and 111, yes. Please proceed, meanwhile --
